requirements.title: Formatted records are representable character sequences
requirements.definition: A formatted record consists of a sequence of characters representable in the processor.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

S12.2.2-001 I/O records/files runtime fixtures: the internal formatted WRITE produces exact representable characters '137 Q' in a length-five record prefilled with '#', and a formatted READ recovers 137 and 'Q' into nondefault sentinels.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.

S12.2.2-001 I/O records/files fixture boundaries: These fixtures are single-image positive runtime observations over internal CHARACTER files, scratch external files, and conservative local named files created in the execution working directory and deleted by the program. They assert only exact integers/logicals/characters, LEN before character equality, IOSTAT zero, and equality with the named IOSTAT_END constant. They do not assert byte sizes, record marker layout, IOMSG text, numeric IOSTAT values, ambient file existence, path syntax beyond the chosen local names, preconnected file identity, coarray image interactions, stream/record correspondence, or required diagnostics for mismatched forms/nonexistent files. Remaining facets stay pending with their source-accounting rationale.

requirements.title: Processors may prohibit some control characters in formatted records
requirements.definition: A processor may prohibit some control characters from appearing in a formatted record.

pending.formatted-control-character-prohibition-: No portable oracle exists for which control characters, if any, are prohibited; future tests must not require acceptance or rejection of a particular control character except where another rule fixes it.

requirements.title: Formatted record length is measured in characters and primarily depends on written characters
requirements.definition: The length of a formatted record is measured in characters and depends primarily on the number of characters put into the record when it is written.

requirements.title: Formatted records are read or written only by formatted input/output statements
requirements.definition: Formatted records shall be read or written only by formatted input/output statements.

requirements.title: Formatted record length has processor/media latitude and may be zero
requirements.definition: Formatted record length may depend on the processor and external medium, and may be zero.

pending.formatted-length-processor-or-medium-dep: No portable oracle may assert an external formatted record length when the processor or medium can affect it; future tests use internal records for exact character counts.
